page: Amazon Web Services r7g.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Graviton3 processor family, specifically the Neoverse-V1 model running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance profiles. The r7g.large demonstrates average single-core capabilities, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores. However, because it features only two physical cores without hyperthreading, its multi-core scaling is limited, resulting in weak multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is mixed; while large-block read-only memory bandwidth is average, small-block cached reads and large-block write speeds fall into the weak category. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-accelerated AES instructions, though overall Passmark CPU and extended instruction scores remain low.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7g.large leverages the ARM64 Graviton architecture to deliver a high memory footprint per vCPU at a lower resource cost compared to traditional x86-based memory-optimized instances. This makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. Suitable workloads include medium-sized caching layers, Redis key-value stores, lightweight database operations, and memory-bound utility applications that benefit from a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.
